sections.title: At Home
sections.content: Describing a home needs no new grammar — it needs 'hay', which you met in Lesson 4, and the words for what is in the place. Spanish gives you two ways to say the same thing: 'hay un sofá' points at what is there, and 'tenemos un sofá' says whose it is. Both are ordinary; 'hay' is the neutral one.

sections.title: Furniture, and what is lying around

items.spanish: Hay una sala de estar, una cocina, un dormitorio y un baño.
items.english: There's a living room, a kitchen, a bedroom and a bathroom.

items.spanish: Aquí tenemos un sofá, una mesa pequeña y una estantería.
items.english: Here we have a sofa, a small table and a bookshelf.

items.spanish: En el frigorífico solo hay leche y fruta.
items.english: There's only milk and fruit in the fridge.

items.spanish: En la mesa hay una lista de cosas para la cocina.
items.english: On the table there's a list of things for the kitchen.

sections.content: 'El sofá' keeps its masculine article even though it ends in -á, and 'la mesa' is feminine as its -a suggests. When a word looks like an exception, learn it with its article and stop worrying about the rule.
